performed_via_github_app.name: Welcome
performed_via_github_app.description: > a GitHub App built with [probot](https://github.com/probot/probot) that welcomes new users based off maintainer defined comments that should be located in a `.github/config.yml` The 3 plugins it combines with are [new-issue-welcome] ### New Issue Welcome: [new-issue-welcome](https://github.com/behaviorbot/new-issue-welcome) ### New PR Welcome: [new-pr-welcome](https://github.com/behaviorbot/new-pr-welcome) and [first-pr-merge](https://github.com/behaviorbot/new-issue-welcome) ## Usage 1. Install the bot on the intended repositories. The plugin requires the following **Permissions and Events**: - Pull requests: **Read & Write** - Issues: **Read & Write** 2. Create a `config.yml` file to check for content of the comments: ``` yaml # Configuration for welcome - https://github.com/behaviorbot/welcome # Configuration for new-issue-welcome - https://github.com/behaviorbot/new-issue-welcome # Comment to be posted to on first time issues newIssueWelcomeComment: > Thanks for opening your first issue here! Be sure to follow the issue template! # Configuration for new-pr-welcome - https://github.com/behaviorbot/new-pr-welcome # Comment to be posted to on PRs from first time contributors in your repository newPRWelcomeComment: > Thanks for opening this pull request! Please check out our contributing guidelines. # Configuration for first-pr-merge - https://github.com/behaviorbot/first-pr-merge # Comment to be posted to on pull requests merged by a first time user firstPRMergeComment: > Congrats on merging your first pull request! We here at behaviorbot are proud of you! # It is recommend to include as many gifs and emojis as possible ``` You can opt out of having the bot comment on first time pull requests, pull request merges, or new issues by not filling in a value for each app's respective field.

issue.title: 🩹 Fix: Middleware/CORS Remove Scheme Restriction

repository.name: fiber
repository.description: ⚡️ Express inspired web framework written in Go

issue.body:
# Description

The Fiber CORS middleware unnecessarily restricts the scheme for the origins that can be configured. As already stated [here](https://github.com/gofiber/fiber/issues/3160#issuecomment-2402456061), the CORS spec does not define any restrictions on the scheme. However, the Fiber CORS middleware restricts the scheme to `http` or `https`.

Fixes #3160

## Changes introduced

Removes the scheme restriction of the CORS middleware configuration.
